name: arc-concentric-frame-reversal
description: Use when ARC grids contain nested rectangular color bands. Reverse the color order from outermost to innermost, preserving geometry and background.
---

# ARC: Reverse nested frame colors

## Trigger
Use when a grid contains one or more axis-aligned nested rectangular frames/bands, and demonstrations show that colors are reassigned by reversing the sequence of concentric layers.

## Procedure
1. Identify each independent nested rectangular motif and its outer-to-inner sequence of color bands. Treat the outside background as unchanged.
2. For each motif, record the original sequence `[c0, c1, ..., cn]`, where `c0` is the outermost colored band and `cn` is the innermost region.
3. Recolor the same cells using the reversed sequence: outermost gets `cn`, next band gets `c(n-1)`, ..., innermost gets `c0`. Geometry and all cell boundaries remain fixed.
4. Apply the operation independently to every motif. Different motifs may have different numbers of layers; the same reversal rule still applies.
5. Verify by checking each nested band against its counterpart from the opposite end of the sequence, and ensure background/zero cells are unchanged.

## Evidence pattern
A demonstration with four layers `[8, 7, 4, 3]` transformed to `[3, 4, 7, 8]`, while a three-layer motif `[2, 1, 3]` transformed to `[3, 1, 2]`. Thus this is reversal within each motif, not a fixed global color substitution.",
